summary_en: This phase I/II pilot study tests memory-like natural killer (ML NK) cells given after a TCRαβ-depleted haploidentical stem cell transplant in people with high-risk acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Patients receive conditioning drugs before a donor stem cell graft on day 0, ML NK cells on day +7, and IL-2 under the skin on 7 doses every other day through day +19. The study's main objective is to establish the safety and feasibility of generating and infusing ML NK cells.
summary_es: Este estudio piloto de fase I/II evalúa las células asesinas naturales de memoria (ML NK) administradas después de un trasplante de células madre haploidénticas con depleción de linfocitos T TCRαβ, en personas con leucemia mieloide aguda (LMA) de alto riesgo. Los pacientes reciben medicamentos de acondicionamiento antes de un injerto de células madre del donante el día 0, células ML NK el día +7 e IL-2 por vía subcutánea en 7 dosis, cada dos días, hasta el día +19. El objetivo principal del estudio es establecer la seguridad y la viabilidad de generar y administrar las células ML NK.
who_for: Adults up to 40 years old with high-risk AML in remission, morphologic leukemia-free state, or refractory or multiply relapsed disease.
Karnofsky (age 16 and older) or Lansky (under 16) performance status above 60%.
Adequate liver, kidney, heart and lung function, as defined in the criteria.
Has an available familial haploidentical donor willing to give two leukapheresis collections.
Able to give informed consent, or has a guardian who can consent.
not_for: Active graft-versus-host disease, or prior GvHD without being off immunosuppression for at least 3 months.
Currently receiving other investigational agents at the time of transplant.
Active central nervous system or extramedullary disease.
Allergy to compounds similar to study agents, or inability to stop medicines such as glucocorticoids.
